I've been working this land for 50 years. My father farmed here before me, and I know this soil, I know Quzhou's weather. I don't need to think too hard about this — I follow what has worked.

My 7 mu rotates wheat and maize on the same plots. Wheat goes in the ground in October after I finish maize harvest. Maize goes in after wheat is cut in June. Same land, used twice a year, every year.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved seed from the village cooperative — the variety that's been popular around here for several years. I trust it. I'll rotary till after maize harvest to turn in the stubble, then sow. I irrigate before it freezes, again at jointing in March, and once more at heading. Three times is what this crop needs with well water. I'll spray aphids and powdery mildew in spring — usually two rounds. Fertilizer: compound base fertilizer at sowing, urea top-dressed at jointing. I've settled on amounts that don't waste money but don't starve the crop either.

For maize, I use hybrid seed — everyone switched to hybrids years ago and the yields are much better. After wheat harvest I plant directly without tilling. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate at emergence if it's dry, and again around tasseling. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. Corn borer is the main pest — I spray once if I see the signs.

Three people in my household, 7 mu — this system feeds us and gives us something to sell. I'm not changing what works.
